h: When the Town Goes Festival Crazy
p: Cheltenham is famous for its festivals, and when they're on, the town transforms. The big jump racing festival in March brings huge crowds, while the literature, jazz and science festivals add their own buzz through the year. If your visit falls during one of these, expect busy streets and packed restaurants, and get your oche booked well before you travel. Outside festival time, it's a relaxed and easy-going spot for a group night out.

New to darts? Don't worry, it's easier than it looks. Stand side-on, keep your elbow steady and use your forearm for a smooth throw. Release the dart with a gentle flick and follow through. And remember, the scoring is automatic, so all you need to do is aim and enjoy it.

For a group, it's worth deciding beforehand whether you want a competitive evening or just a laugh. Flight Club's game formats cater for both, and the luck-based ones are brilliant for keeping beginners in the game.

Cheltenham has plenty more to explore. The Wilson, the town's art gallery and museum, is a great free stop with a mix of exhibitions. Imperial Gardens, next to the Town Hall, is a pretty spot full of flowers in the summer months. If you fancy a trip out, the Cotswolds are right on the doorstep, with honey-coloured villages and rolling hills to explore. Cleeve Hill, just outside town, gives you sweeping views over the area and makes a fine morning walk before an evening of darts.
